narrative.overview:
The site is a reference book for reading technology in the city. Like a good field guide, it is organised into entries you can look up, each with an identifier, an icon and a plain description, and it is laid out to be consulted outdoors by someone who is not an expert. The page is warm paper marked with a dot grid; content sits on white sheets with a hairline outline; identifiers are set in monospace and section labels in small capitals. The one flourish is an italic serif headline at the top of a page, the way a guide's title page is set differently from its entries.

The mood is civic, trustworthy, calm and clear. Density is moderate on the marketing pages and tight inside the taxonomy explorer, where three panes behave like an index, a list and an entry. Hand-drawn material is rare: the exploded city plan in the home hero, and the sketched vision mocks, which no page places at present. Those are the guide's plates, drawn in pen, and the mocks are labelled as illustrations.

This system rejects three looks. It is not SaaS marketing gloss: no gradients, glass cards, glowing accents or hero metrics. It is not smart-city futurism: no dark dashboards, neon data lines or surveillance-tech styling. It is not government-portal drab: no grey boxes, dense link lists or bureaucratic form styling.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper with a 24px dot grid as the substrate; white sheets with slate hairlines for anything that is read at length.
Navy does the work. Medium blue is the hover and the "digital" tone. Chartreuse is held back for live data.
Public Sans everywhere, one italic serif headline per page, monospace for identifiers.
Small radii (4px controls, 6px sheets); full pills only for chips and tags.
Three levels of depth: paper, sheet, lifted.
Light theme only. Colour mode switching is disabled.
Motion is brief, state-driven, and turned off under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Live Data Rule
rules.body: Chartreuse marks live data and nothing else. Never text, borders, hover states or decoration.

rules.name: The Hover Is Blue Rule
rules.body: Navy is the resting state; medium blue is the response. An interactive navy element answers a pointer by turning medium blue, not by darkening.

rules.name: The Sketch Stays In The Sketch Rule
rules.body: Teal, gold, coral and sketch ink never leave the vision mocks.

rules.name: The One Serif Line Rule
rules.body: Italic serif appears once per page, in the hero. Upright serif is allowed only for entry names in the taxonomy.

rules.name: The Identifier Rule
rules.body: If a string could be pasted into the API, it is set in Source Code Pro.

rules.name: The Twelve Pixel Floor Rule
rules.body: No text below 0.75rem, including inside mocks.

rules.name: The Outline First Rule
rules.body: A shadow never stands alone. Every raised surface also carries a 1px rule outline, so the edge holds on low-contrast displays.

rules.name: The Lift Means Link Rule
rules.body: Only surfaces that go somewhere rise on hover. Static cards stay at sheet level.

dos: Do put running prose and navigation on a white sheet with a 1px rule outline and the sheet shadow. Only headings and short ledes sit on the dot grid.
Do use navy (#1B2B80) for primary actions and medium blue (#2563D0) for their hover.
Do keep targets at 44px or taller, and give every focusable element a solid navy outline.
Do set ids, schema versions and anything copyable in Source Code Pro.
Do open a feature section with the section header: rule, label, headline, lede.
Do honour reduced motion on every transition, and keep motion to 200ms or 300ms on state changes.
Do caption vision mocks as illustrations of fictional services.
donts: Don't use chartreuse for text, borders, hover states or decoration.
Don't set more than one italic serif line on a page.
Don't use Kalam, dashed borders, irregular radii or the sketch palette outside the vision mocks.
Don't use gradients, glass cards, glows or hero metrics.
Don't build dark dashboards, neon data lines or surveillance-tech visuals.
Don't fall back to grey boxes, dense link lists or bureaucratic form styling.
Don't lift a card on hover unless it links somewhere.
Don't set caution orange (#C2410C) as text; use the darker caution text step.
Don't add a dark theme. The tokens are light only.
Don't credit Superbloom, or present any steward other than Helpful Places.
